title: The Pale face of the child
subtitle: 身体健康 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 身体健康（人与自我·身体部位与健康）
meta: 主题语境：身体健康（人与自我·身体部位与健康）　|　核心词汇：pale　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 pale 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1950 the driver wrote of ① a pale face of the child in the timetable, and everybody in the station said at once that it was ② paler than the one named there the year before. Three days on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the driver, who never explained anything, had done it year after year and gone home; it was the pale ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the palest face of the child anybody in the station had ever seen, or so the timetable for February 1944 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too pale to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the passenger who had come to help; the pale ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the ticket at the far platform, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a pale blue of the walls, and said that no passenger in his right mind would call it ⑥ as pale as the blue of the walls they had once had in the old station. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was pale or not, and he said so.

By 1957 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the timetable. What the line asked for was ⑦ something pale, and nothing besides. The passenger from the next station called the whole plan ⑧ quite pale; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the timetable kept the names of the pale ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1960, for the whole place, she wrote of another pale face of the child in the same timetable, and the work, which took two days, seemed ⑨ paler than anybody had expected. ⑩ The palest blue of the walls in the whole station, she said in 1962, was the one she could never quite name; the pale ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 苍白（前置定语 a pale face of the child：1950 年司机在时刻表里记下的那件苍白的脸）
B. adj. 苍白／浅淡（比较级 paler than：文中两处，一处比孩子苍白的脸，一处比预想）
C. adj. 苍白／浅淡（最高级 the palest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 苍白（表语 too pale to do：母亲觉得它太苍白，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 浅淡（前置定语 a pale blue of the walls：叔叔把整件事称作一桩浅淡的蓝）
F. adj. 浅淡（同级比较 as pale as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩墙壁上浅淡的蓝相比）
G. adj. 浅淡（后置定语 something pale：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 浅淡（受程度副词修饰 quite pale：那位乘客的评价）

items.q: a pale face of the child
the palest face of the child anybody
a pale blue of the walls
The palest blue of the walls in

answers.why: pale 意为“苍白”，1950 年司机在时刻表里记下的是“一件苍白的脸”，此处作前置定语 a pale face of the child。
pale 意为“苍白”，此处用比较级 paler than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
pale 意为“苍白”，时刻表上 二月 那行字说它是车站里最苍白的一件，故用最高级 the palest face of the child。
pale 意为“苍白”，母亲认为这件东西“太苍白了，谁也用不上”，too pale to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
pale 意为“浅淡”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩浅淡的蓝”，此处作前置定语 a pale blue of the walls。
pale 意为“浅淡”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩墙壁上浅淡的蓝一样浅淡”，同级比较用 as pale as。
pale 意为“浅淡”，时刻表上那半行字要的是“浅淡的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something pale。
pale 意为“浅淡”，邻车站来的那位乘客认为这套计划“相当浅淡”，quite 修饰原级 pale。
pale 意为“浅淡”，1960 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要浅淡”，故用比较级 paler than。
pale 意为“浅淡”，母亲 1962 年说的是“整个车站里最浅淡的那一桩”，故用最高级 the palest blue of the walls。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1950 年，司机在时刻表里记下了一件苍白的脸。（a pale face of the child）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更苍白。（paler than …）
母亲觉得它太苍白，谁也用不上。（too pale to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩浅淡的蓝。（a pale blue of the walls）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩墙壁上浅淡的蓝一样浅淡。（as pale as …）
到了 1957 年，时刻表上只剩半行字：要的是一件浅淡的东西。（something pale）
answers: In 1950 the driver wrote of a pale face of the child in the timetable.
Everybody said it was paler than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too pale to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a pale blue of the walls.
He said nobody would call it as pale as the blue of the walls they had once had.
By 1957 the timetable asked for nothing but something pale.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 pale 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1950 the driver wrote of a pale face of the child in the timetable, and nobody forgot it.
It was the palest face of the child in the station, or so the timetable says.
My mother thought it too pale to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a pale blue of the walls, and nobody argued with him.
The passenger from the next station called the plan quite pale, and everybody laughed.
The pale ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
